# Prism plugin index

12 bundled plugins plus one official installable catalog. `index.json` is also the data source for the in-app
"Plugin marketplace"; the two tables below are generated by `tools/make_plugin_index.py` from the
**plugin source + index.json**, so do not edit the table contents by hand
(re-run the script after changing them, or use `--check` to see whether they are up to date).

Built-in plugins provide zh/en/ja names, parameter labels and descriptions. Third-party
plugins that only provide a Chinese string keep showing it as-is; plugins may opt in by
supplying `{"zh","en","ja"}` objects (see `docs/plugin-api.en.md`).

Parameter defaults are defined by `PARAMS` in the source. After you save, Prism hot-reloads automatically in about 1.5 seconds.

- In-app entry: plugin window → "Plugin marketplace". Browse plugins, check their "Installed / Update available / Not installed"
  status, and install or update with one click.
- Catalog URL: `https://11ly322.github.io/Prism/plugins/index.json` (source in the repository at `plugins/index.json`,
  copied to `docs/plugins/index.json` on release).
- Every entry carries a SHA-256. After download, **only the AST is parsed, no code is executed**; the confirmation dialog
  shows the author and the capability declarations, and files are written to disk only after you confirm.
- To use your own catalog: set the environment variable `PRISM_PLUGIN_CATALOG` to point at your `index.json`.
  See [docs/plugin-api.md](../docs/plugin-api.en.md) for the schema.
- If the online catalog cannot be fetched, the app uses the cache from the last successful fetch (`plugin_catalog.json`,
  in the same directory as the settings file) and marks it as "Offline cache" in the window.

## Installing plugins

Three ways, same result:

1. **Plugin marketplace** (9.5.0): plugin window → "Plugin marketplace" → pick one → "Install" / "Update".
2. **Install from URL**: plugin window → "Install from URL…" → enter a direct http(s) link to the `.py`; you can also enter a SHA-256.
3. **Drop into the folder**: put the `.py` into the plugin folder (the plugin window shows the full path at the top), then click "Rescan" or wait 1.5 seconds for hot reload.

Temporarily disable: rename `xxx.py` to `xxx.py.disabled`, and the plugin window shows an "Enable xxx" button.

Installation only guarantees that what was downloaded has not been modified (SHA-256); it does **not** guarantee that the author is trustworthy.
The `network` / `writes_files` a plugin declares are shown in the confirmation dialog, but they are only declarations the author filled in.

## Publishing a plugin to the marketplace

The official marketplace reads `plugins/index.json`. From writing a plugin to users seeing it in the marketplace, there are six steps:

1. **Write the plugin**: put the single file in `docs/plugins/<filename>.py`, using an ASCII filename.
   In `PLUGIN`, `id` must be unique and `api` must be `2`; fill in `network` / `writes_files` truthfully;
   for `PARAMS` use `slider` / `select` / `checkbox` / `text`.
2. **Test locally**: put the `.py` into the plugin folder (the plugin window shows the full path at the top), run it, tune parameters, and save the result;
   starting with `--plugin-dev` lets you see load/run times in `logs/plugins.log`.
3. **Compute the SHA-256** (must match the file byte for byte):
   ~~~powershell
   Get-FileHash docs\plugins\myplugin.py -Algorithm SHA256
   ~~~
4. **Add an entry to `plugins/index.json`** (`plugins` array, schema 1):

   ~~~json
   {
     "id": "myplugin",
     "name": {"zh": "我的插件", "en": "My plugin", "ja": "マイプラグイン"},
     "version": "1.0",
     "api": 2,
     "author": "你的名字",
     "description": {"zh": "一句话说明", "en": "One line", "ja": "ひとこと"},
     "network": false,
     "writes_files": false,
     "url": "https://11ly322.github.io/Prism/plugins/myplugin.py",
     "sha256": "<上一步的 64 位小写十六进制>",
     "source": "docs/plugins/myplugin.py"
   }
   ~~~

   The filename in `url` must match `source`; the official catalog always uses the Pages address.
5. **Generate the index and self-check**:

   ~~~bash
   python tools/make_plugin_index.py          # update the README tables in all three languages + the docs copy
   python tools/make_plugin_index.py --check  # must pass
   ~~~

   It validates the SHA-256, the trilingual fields, `id` uniqueness, `api` and the URL, and confirms that `docs/plugins/index.json`
   matches the repository version. The release gate also runs this step.
6. **Open a PR**: commit the source, `plugins/index.json`, `plugins/README.md` (three files, one per language) and
   `docs/plugins/index.json` together. After merging, the Pages deployment takes effect in about 1 minute;
   click "Refresh" in the app to see the new plugin, and users with an older version installed will see "Update available".

Updating a published plugin: edit the source in `docs/plugins/` → bump the version by 1 (keep `PLUGIN.version` and the
`version` in `index.json` in sync) → recompute the SHA-256 → run the generator script. The marketplace decides whether an update is available by version number.

**Maintaining your own marketplace (outside the official repository)**:

- Put an `index.json` in the same format on any static http(s) host (every entry must still carry a SHA-256);
- users set the environment variable `PRISM_PLUGIN_CATALOG` to point at it **before starting Prism**;
- no code changes and no repackaging are needed.

Security bottom line: the catalog itself executes no code; on install the app only parses the AST and strictly compares the SHA-256,
and writes to disk only after you confirm.

## Parameters are remembered (9.4.0)

Each plugin's parameters are stored in the settings file by `id` (`plugin_params`). The next time the same plugin runs, the previous values are restored automatically,
including after restarting Prism. Clicking "Restore defaults" in the result window clears this memory.

- The plugin changes a parameter range: out-of-range values are clamped to the new range.
- The plugin removes an option: the now-invalid option falls back to the new default.
- The plugin changes its `id`: it counts as a new plugin, and the old memory is not applied.

## Development workflow

1. Copy `_template.py` to `myplugin.py` (do not start the filename with an underscore; that is reserved for framework files)
2. Change `PLUGIN` / `PARAMS` / `run`
3. Save; Prism hot-reloads automatically in about 1.5 seconds (you can also click "Reload plugins" in the plugin window)
4. Errors do not crash the main app: they are written to `logs/plugins.log` and the app falls back to the original image

## Three control types

| type | Required fields | Type passed to run | Legacy form (still supported) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| slider | min / max / default, optional step | float | omit type or write range |
| select | options / default | str | type=choice + choices |
| checkbox | default | bool | type=bool |
| text | default (may be an empty string) | str | none (added in 8.3.0) |

## PLUGIN fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | yes | Unique identifier; used for parameter memory, the install filename, and the marketplace catalog. Prefer ASCII letters and digits plus `-` `_` |
| name | yes | Name shown in the list |
| version | recommended | Shown after the name; the marketplace uses it to decide whether an update is available |
| api | recommended | 1 and 2 are currently supported; `2` is the `run(img, **params)` form |
| author | recommended | Shown in the hover tooltip |
| description | recommended | Shown in the hover tooltip |
| network | recommended | Whether it uses the network; fill in truthfully |
| writes_files | recommended | Whether it writes files; fill in truthfully |

## How to add third-party plugins

- Single file, depending only on Pillow and numpy (both shipped with Prism); do not spawn threads and do not modify Prism's internal state.
- Use an ASCII filename and a unique `id`; do not start with `_`.
- Put your own plugins in the user plugin folder (the plugin window shows the full path at the top); do not modify the bundled plugins in the install directory.
- To get into the official catalog: open a PR adding an entry to `plugins/index.json`, put the source in `docs/plugins/`,
  and fill in `source`, `url`, `sha256` plus the zh/en/ja names and descriptions; `make_plugin_index.py --check` must pass.
- Plugins with network / file-writing side effects must declare them truthfully in `PLUGIN`.

## Reusable functions

`_utils.py` provides `preview_then_export` / `downscale_if_needed` / `upscale_back` / `preserve_alpha` /
`split_alpha` / `to_rgb` / `clamp_params`; it is not part of the framework, so copying it out also works.
`preview_then_export(func, img)` is the easiest: downscale → run func → scale back to the original size → paste the alpha back.
Before importing, add the plugin folder to `sys.path` (see the header comment in that file).
